gaps.sentence: If the strike goes ___, deliveries will stop nationwide.
Do you get ___ well with your new colleagues?
gaps.explanation: get on (with) = have a good relationship; also get along with (AmE).

gaps.sentence: I can't make ___ what the sign says from here.
gaps.explanation: make out = see, hear or understand with difficulty.

gaps.sentence: After twenty years of smoking, he finally managed to give it ___.
gaps.explanation: give up = stop/quit (a habit or attempt).

gaps.sentence: The caterpillar will turn ___ a butterfly.

gaps.explanation: bring down = cause a government/person to lose power; reduce (prices).

gaps.sentence: The concert tickets sold ___ within an hour.
gaps.explanation: sell out = all tickets/goods are sold.

gaps.sentence: They get ___ on very little money.
gaps.explanation: get by = manage to survive (with difficulty).
